In Step 1, the Planner correctly identified that onshore winds bring moist air which enhances coastal precipitation. However, in Step 3, after reviewing the Britannica page which explicitly stated that sea breezes "foster the development of clouds" and "produce showers," the Planner erroneously concluded that the dominant effect is "coastal cooling" and "suppression of convection." This contradicts the Britannica text provided in the same turn and general meteorological principles where moist onshore winds (especially in tropical/subtropical regions) are a primary driver of coastal rainfall, not just cooling. The Planner's decision to pursue option C (cold temperatures) instead of reinforcing option A (heavier rainfall) was a reasoning error at this step.
